rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duty to spare a treatyless polytheist remains whenever there is hope that hearing the truth will guide him; killing is warranted only after hope ends.
rows.anchor: ولازم ذلك الإعتناء التام بكل طريق يرجى فيه الوصول إلى هداية ضال والفوز بإحياء حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a polytheist seeks protection to examine the true call, the believer must secure him until he hears God’s word, then return him safely so he can choose freely.
rows.anchor: فإذا استجار المشرك لينظر فيما تندب إليه الدعوة الحقة ويتبعها إن اتضحت له كان من الواجب إجارته حتى يسمع كلام الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once he persists in error after the proof, his protection ends and he may be killed by whatever means is easiest.
rows.anchor: فإذا تمادى بعد ذلك في ضلاله وأصر في استكباره صار ممن ارتفع عنه الأمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse qualifies the preceding general command to kill polytheists wherever found.
rows.anchor: وقد بان بما قدمناه أولا أن الآية مخصصة لعموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing God’s word sets the limit of the asylum: after the seeker can distinguish guidance from error, he must be returned to his own safe place.
rows.anchor: { حتى يسمع كلام الله } غاية للاستجارة والاجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s word means the Qur’an generally, with relevant passages chosen to explain divine knowledge, religion, and the seeker’s doubts; restricting it to monotheism, Bara’a, or its opening seasonal verses lacks evidence.
rows.anchor: وبذلك يظهر فساد ما قيل إن المراد بكلام الله آيات التوحيد من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing means understanding religion’s foundations; for a non-Arab who cannot understand Arabic, the goal is comprehension rather than listening to Arabic recitation itself.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بسمع كلام الله الوقوف على أصول الدين ومعالمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruling is decisive and remains un-abrogated: accountability and severity come only after the proof is made clear.
rows.anchor: فالآية محكمة غير قابلة للنسخ إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that 9:6 was abrogated by the command to fight all polytheists is false; 9:6 remains binding until the end of time.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر فساد قول من قال أن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse protects someone seeking asylum for a religious purpose that may benefit his faith; it does not establish a general right of refuge for unrelated reasons.
rows.anchor: الآية إنما توجب إجارة المستجير إذا استجار لأمر ديني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction to escort the seeker safely preserves freedom in his life and choices, leaving people accountable on clear evidence after the messengers.
rows.anchor: التحفظ على حرية الناس في حياتهم وأعمالهم الحيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also supports that belief in religion’s foundations must rest on certain knowledge, not even strong probability.
rows.anchor: الاعتقاد بأصل الدين أن يكون عن علم يقيني لا يداخله شك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s announced rule was that only he or a man from him could deliver a message on his behalf.
rows.anchor: لا إن الله أمرني لا يؤدي عني إلا أنا أو رجل مني

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi reports from Hurayz that the Prophet first sent Abu Bakr with Bara’a, then Jibril said only Ali should deliver it, so the Prophet sent Ali to catch Abu Bakr and recite it in Mecca.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن حريز عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام أن رسول الله بعث أبا بكر مع براءة إلى الموسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four-month period fixes the term for treaties with no stated duration; treaties already given a term remain valid until that term expires.
rows.anchor: المراد تعيين المدة للعهود التي لا مدة لها

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Basir reports that Ali announced on the Day of Sacrifice that naked circumambulation and polytheist pilgrimage were forbidden, and that treaty holders kept their stated term while untimed treaties received four months.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسيري العياشي والمجمع عن أبى بصير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال خطب علي عليه السلام بالناس

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s answer to Abu Bakr in the preceding report was that only he or a man from him could deliver on his behalf.
rows.anchor: يا أبا بكر إنه لا يؤدي عني إلا أنا أو رجل مني

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafi reports that Jibril reserved delivery for the Prophet or a man from him; Ali caught Abu Bakr between Mecca and Medina and recited the passage at the pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: وفيه اخرج ابن مردويه عن أبي رافع رضي الله عنه قال بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا بكر

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that Ali took Bara’a from Abu Bakr; the Prophet reassured Abu Bakr that he remained his brother and companion, while only a man from the Prophet could deliver this message.
rows.anchor: وفيه اخرج ابن حبان وابن مردويه عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا بكر

rows.speaker: ابن شهر آشوب
rows.claim: Ibn Shahr Ashub cites a broad set of transmitters and authorities for the account that Ali took the passage from Abu Bakr after Jibril’s instruction.
rows.anchor: وقد نقل في تفسير البرهان عن ابن شهر آشوب أنه رواه الطبرسي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The compiled report attributed to Ibn Abbas says that after nine verses of Bara’a were revealed, Jibril directed the Prophet to send Ali to take the passage from Abu Bakr, who returned distressed at being recalled.
rows.anchor: قال ولما رجع أبو بكر إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جزع وقال يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s appointment of Ali and removal of Abu Bakr from this delivery followed Jibril’s unrestricted instruction; no report restricts it to Bara’a or treaty annulment.
rows.anchor: إحداهما أن بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عليا ببراءة وعزله أبا بكر إنما كان بأمر من ربه بنزول جبرئيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali also announced the treaty deadlines, the ban on naked circumambulation, and the ban on polytheist pilgrimage, all rulings grounded in Qur’anic verses.
rows.anchor: كان ينادي بحكم آخر وهو أن من كان له مدة فهو إلى مدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some narrations add that Ali announced that only a believer enters Paradise; the author considers this implausible because many earlier Meccan and Medinan verses had already made it known.
rows.anchor: لا يدخل الجنه إلا مؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali’s mission therefore covered Bara’a and three or four additional Qur’anic rulings, all within Jibril’s instruction that only the Prophet or a man from him deliver them.
rows.anchor: لم تكن رسالة علي عليه السلام مقصورة على تأدية آيات براءة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report judged good by al-Tirmidhi says Abu Bakr and Ali went together, then Ali announced the treaty notice and related prohibitions during the days of Tashriq.
rows.anchor: فانطلقا فحجا فقام علي رضي الله عنه في أيام التشريق فنادى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several Sunni routes say Abu Bakr led the pilgrimage while Ali announced Bara’a; Shia reports instead say Ali also held the pilgrimage command, which the author sees as possibly supported by reports of his judicial duties.
rows.anchor: ورد في عدة من طرق أهل السنة أن النبي استعمل أبا بكر على الحج عامه ذلك فكان هو أمير الحاج وعلي ينادي ببراءة

rows.speaker: الحسن عن علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says Ali hesitated because he was not eloquent, but the Prophet promised God would strengthen his speech and guide his heart, then instructed him to announce the passage and hear both sides before judging.
rows.anchor: يا نبي الله إني لست بلسن ولا بخطيب قال صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يأبى الله ما بي إلا أن أذهب بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The version saying Ali was sent to Yemen is suspect: Bara’a’s wording clearly addresses Mecca at the Greater Pilgrimage, so Yemen likely replaced an original reference to Mecca.
rows.anchor: إلا أن اشتمال الرواية على لفظ اليمن يسيء الظن بها إذ من البين من لفظ آيات براءة أنها مقرة على أهل مكة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says he accompanied Ali to announce four rules: no naked circumambulation, no joint Muslim and polytheist pilgrimage after that year, treaty holders keep their covenant, and God and His Messenger disavow the polytheists.
rows.anchor: بعث عليا بأربع لا يطوف بالبيت عريان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra’s reports have differing wordings and textual problems, though the version previously cited is the strongest in wording among them.
rows.anchor: وأمتن الروايات متنا هذه التي أوردناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A version adding that only believers enter Paradise is strained because that teaching had appeared in many verses for years; its four-month treaty wording also conflicts with Qur’anic and better-attested reports.
rows.anchor: وقد سبق أنه نزلت في معناه آيات كثيرة مكية ومدنية منذ سنين

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In the Bukhari-Muslim account, Abu Bakr’s callers announced at Mina on the Day of Sacrifice that polytheists could no longer make pilgrimage and naked circumambulation was forbidden; Ali joined to announce Bara’a and repeat those rules.
rows.anchor: أخرج البخاري ومسلم وابن المنذر وابن مردويه والبيهقي في الدلائل عن أبي هريرة قال بعثني أبو بكر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Another wording has Ali and Abu Hurayra announce that only Muslims enter Paradise, treaty holders remain protected to their term, and polytheists may not return to pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه قال كنت مع علي حين بعثه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى مكة ببراءة فكنا ننادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revealed phrase that only the Prophet or a man from him may deliver on his behalf is general, covering Bara’a and any divine ruling he must newly convey himself.
rows.anchor: وكيفما كان فهو كلام مطلق يشمل تأدية براءة وكل حكم إلهي احتاج النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إلى أن يؤديه عنه مؤد غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the pilgrimage bans and treaty deadlines are divine rulings, there is no reason Abu Bakr or Abu Hurayra alone would announce them while Ali repeatedly delivered them.
rows.anchor: فما معنى إرجاع أمرها إلى أبي بكر أو نداء أبي هريرة بها وحده

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and similar commentators restrict the delivery rule to Bara’a, arguing that Arab custom reserved treaty annulment for the contracting party or a close relative, which is why Ali replaced Abu Bakr for the announcement.
rows.anchor: نعم أبدع بعض المفسرين كإبن كثير وأترابه هنا وجها وجهوا به ما تتضمنه هذه الروايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported custom-based explanation says Abu Bakr remained pilgrimage leader and had other callers, including Abu Hurayra, while Ali was one of the people assigned to announce the rulings.
rows.anchor: وكان علي أحد من عنده لهذا الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says commentators have conflated Qur’anic interpretation, assessment of report reliability, and theological debates about whether Abu Bakr or Ali was superior or led the pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: الذي ينبغي أن يقال بالنظر إليه إنهم أخطأوا في هذا التوجيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delivery phrase plainly covers any divine message the Prophet himself was obliged to deliver; routine delegations to rulers or other people conveyed teachings already publicly transmitted.
rows.anchor: فالجملة ظاهرة أتم ظهور في أن ما كان على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يؤديه لا يجوز أن يؤديه إلا هو أو رجل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction is between a new, initial divine decree addressed to Meccan polytheists and ordinary messengers sent after the Prophet had conveyed the religion to those present.
rows.anchor: أحكام إلهية ابتدائية لم تبلغ بعد ولم تؤد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says no one delivers on the Prophet’s behalf except himself or a man from him; it concerns duties that are his to perform personally, not every later delegated message.
rows.anchor: لا يؤدي عنك إلا أنت أو رجل منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general duty to pass on teachings does not contradict this rule: those who heard the Prophet were to inform those absent, while targeted messages could later be sent by a letter or envoy.
rows.anchor: ثم إذا مست الحاجة إلى تبليغه بعض من لا وثوق عادة ببلوغ الحكم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claimed Arab custom is unsupported in historical reports, and Islam repeatedly replaced pre-Islamic customs rather than treating them as binding rules.
rows.anchor: تلك السنة العربية التي لا خبر عنها في أيامهم ومغازيهم ولا أثر إلا ما ذكره ابن كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is implausible that the Prophet forgot a supposedly binding custom when first sending Abu Bakr, since it would have been a basic duty he could not ordinarily overlook.
rows.anchor: فهل كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ذهل عنها ونسيها حين أسلم الآيات إلى أبي بكر وأرسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author challenges every proposed basis for the custom: no revealed law establishes it, enemies could not impose it while the Prophet held power, and Abu Hurayra’s announcement would also violate it; such reports are unreliable.
rows.anchor: الحق أن هذه الروايات الحاكية لنداء أبي هريرة وغيره غير سديدة لا ينبغي الركون إليها

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: Al-Manar’s account makes Abu Bakr pilgrimage leader and Ali the envoy who proclaimed the end of untimed covenants, a four-month respite, and the relevant opening verses of Bara’a, assisted by Abu Hurayra and others.
rows.anchor: جملة الروايات تدل على أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم جعل أبا بكر أميرا على الحج سنة تسع

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: Al-Manar accuses some Shia writers of inflating Ali’s merit and using the delivery story to claim his superiority and right to the caliphate.
rows.anchor: إن بعض الشيعة يكبرون هذه المزية لعلي عليه السلام كعادتهم ويضيفون إليها ما لا تصح به رواية

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: Al-Manar cites the public duty to transmit religion, including the Prophet’s instruction that those present tell the absent and his command to convey even one verse.
rows.anchor: ألا فليبلغ الشاهد الغائب

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: Al-Manar says Abu Bakr remained overall pilgrimage leader while Ali handled a special announcement under his authority and with other callers helping.
rows.anchor: والحق أن عليا كرم الله وجهه كان مكلفا بتبليغ أمر خاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says al-Manar misreads the wording as barring all other religious transmission and then narrows it through an unsupported Arab custom; the phrase instead concerns the Prophet’s personal initial delivery.
rows.anchor: لم يحصل معنى كلمة الوحي

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: Al-Manar uses Abu Bakr’s pilgrimage leadership and the Prophet’s later position before death to argue for Abu Bakr’s precedence over the other Companions.
rows.anchor: استدل بإمارة أبي بكر في تلك الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that nobody said Ali led the pilgrimage is false: a Shia report does say so, but the question of leadership does not determine the meaning of the delivery phrase.
rows.anchor: فليس ذلك زعما من البعض ولا بهتانا كما بهته بل رواية روتها الشيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pilgrimage command is a general administrative authority over Muslim society, distinct from the authority to deliver revelation; the Prophet appointed different people to offices without implying comparative merit.
rows.anchor: إنما هي من شعب الولاية الإسلامية العامة التي شأنها التصرف في أمور المجتمع الإسلامي الحيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No political office or social custom can alter, approve, or cancel heavenly revelation; conflating the two lowers divine teaching to ordinary convention.
rows.anchor: وأما الوحي السماوي بما يشتمل عليه من المعارف والشرائع فليس للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ولا لمن دونه صنع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports vary: some have Ali take the verses from Abu Bakr, some distinguish his announcement from Abu Bakr’s pilgrimage command, and some have Abu Bakr direct the proclamation with helpers including Abu Hurayra.
rows.anchor: أنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بعث أبا بكر بالآيات ثم بعث عليا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid’s report says that after returning from Tabuk the Prophet sent Abu Bakr and Ali to proclaim in the markets that treaty holders had four months’ security, after which the general fighting order applied; he had delayed Hajj because polytheists circumambulated naked.
rows.anchor: أقبل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من تبوك حين فرغ منها فأراد الحج ثم قال إنه يحضر البيت مشركون يطوفون عراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports do not establish a universally known account: they disagree over who proclaimed, how many verses were delivered, why Abu Bakr returned, and whether he was recalled after receiving Bara’a.
rows.anchor: فهذا حال الروايات المنقولة عنهم لا يجتمع على كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traditions vary between Ali alone delivering, Abu Bakr sharing the task, and Abu Hurayra or unnamed men joining them; they also count the delivered text from nine verses to the entire surah.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما يحكي إن عليا اختص بتأدية براءة وأخرى تدل على أن أبا بكر شاركه فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports also disagree about the Hajj date, the start of the four-month period, and which sacred months it covered; early exegetes’ opinions are treated as interrupted reports, not settled eyewitness consensus.
rows.anchor: كيف يستقيم دعوى أنه أمر عرفه العام والخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali’s assigned task on that journey was specific, but this does not narrow the broader meaning of the revelation that only the Prophet or a man from him could deliver on his behalf.
rows.anchor: فلا ينبغي الخلط بين ما يدل عليه الكلمة وبين ما أمر به علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that Ali followed Abu Bakr in overall authority rests on Abu Hurayra’s report and similar reports, whose reliability the author has already questioned.
rows.anchor: فأمر استفاده من كلام أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: Al-Manar appeals to an Anas wording, from a man of the Prophet’s household, to deny that the phrase from me means Ali resembles the Prophet or outranks the Companions.
rows.anchor: وهذا النص الصريح يبطل تأويل كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording cited by al-Manar is the same Anas report already presented with variant phrasing from my family or from my household, likely reflecting transmission by meaning.
rows.anchor: هي الرواية السابقة التي أوردناها عن أنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most sound reports preserve the Prophet’s wording that only he or a man from him may deliver; the household phrasing appears in the Anas report, while Abu Saʿid’s version says only the Prophet or Ali.
rows.anchor: وهو يستكثرها إنما هي رواية أنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase from me alone does not establish equivalence in every respect; its force comes from the full wording that no one else may perform the Prophet’s own delivery duty.
rows.anchor: فإن مجرد قول القائل فلان مني لا يدل على تنزيله منزلته في جميع شؤون وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being from someone can signify following rather than full equivalence, as in Abraham’s statement; here the surrounding restriction on delivering for the Prophet supplies the implication that a substitute stands in his place.
rows.anchor: إلا بنوع من القرينة الدالة على عناية كلامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the wording were from my family or household, it would still mean Ali can substitute for the Prophet’s personal delivery; the Prophet also called Abu Bakr his brother and companion.
rows.anchor: لا يؤدي عني إلا رجل من أهلي أو رجل من أهل بيتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Authentic reports identify the Prophet’s household here as Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husayn; among its men only Ali fits, so the phrase points to him.
rows.anchor: أهل بيت النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم هم علي وفاطمة والحسنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating household as all Hashimites or as Hashimites and wives uses ordinary social convention in place of the religious meaning, repeating a linguistic-versus-theological category error.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بأهل بيته عامة اقربائه من بني هاشم أو بنو هاشم ونساؤه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله عليهما السلام
rows.claim: The four months run from 20 Dhu al-Hijjah through Muharram, Safar, Rabiʿ al-Awwal, and the first ten days of Rabiʿ al-Thani; the author says this is abundantly attested from the Imams and also reported by Sunnis.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة وحمران ومحمد بن مسلم عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that Abu Bakr performed Hajj in Dhu al-Qiʿdah lack supporting evidence, so the author sets them aside.
rows.anchor: وهي غير متأيدة ولذلك أغمضنا عنها

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report from Zayn al-Abidin identifies the divinely announced message as the Commander of the Faithful, Ali; other Imami reports and reports attributed to al-Suddi, Abu Malik, and Ibn Abbas give the same interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال الأذان أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to define the Greater Pilgrimage as the Day of Arafah, on which reaching the pilgrimage rites counts as attaining Hajj.
rows.anchor: كان ابن عباس يقول الحج الأكبر يوم عرفة

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali identifies the Greater Pilgrimage as the Day of Sacrifice: if it were Arafah, the four-month notice would last an extra day; he adds that he was the herald among the people.
rows.anchor: قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام الحج الأكبر يوم النحر

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Imam explains that the pilgrimage was called greater because Muslims and polytheists made pilgrimage together that year, and polytheists did not do so afterward.
rows.anchor: إنما سمي الأكبر لأنها كانت سنة حج فيها المسلمون والمشركون

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A separate report from Jaʿfar al-Sadiq says the Greater Pilgrimage is the Day of Sacrifice and the lesser pilgrimage is ʿUmra.
rows.anchor: عن معاوية بن عمار قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن يوم الحج الأكبر فقال يوم النحر والأصغر العمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imami reports, with only rare exceptions, agree that the Greater Pilgrimage day in the verse is the tenth of Dhu al-Hijjah, the Day of Sacrifice, and they transmit this from Ali.
rows.anchor: وقد أطبقت الروايات عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام إلا ما شذ

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Reports through Ibn Abi Awfa and Ibn Umar identify the Day of Sacrifice as the Greater Pilgrimage day.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن أبي أوفى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال يوم الأضحى هذا يوم الحج الأكبر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: The author records alternate identifications of the Greater Pilgrimage day: Arafah (reported from the Prophet, Ali, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn al-Zubayr), the day after Sacrifice according to Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, all pilgrimage days, or the year Abu Bakr led Hajj.
rows.anchor: وقد روي بطرق مختلفة أخرى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه يوم عرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The view that the Greater Pilgrimage means the year Abu Bakr performed Hajj is compatible with the Imam’s explanation that Muslims and polytheists made pilgrimage together that year.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه الأخير لا يأبى الانطباق على ما تقدم من الحديث عن الصادق عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir interprets the end of the sacred months as beginning on the Day of Sacrifice and running through ten days of Rabiʿ al-Thani.
rows.anchor: قال هي يوم النحر إلى عشر مضين من شهر ربيع الآخر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: After the siege of Taif, the Prophet warned that failure to establish prayer and zakat would bring a man from him to strike the fighters and capture their children; the crowd thought of Abu Bakr or Umar, but he took Ali’s hand.
rows.anchor: لتقيمن الصلاة ولتؤتن الزكاة أو لأبعثن عليكم رجلا مني أو كنفسي

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Baqir explains that if they repent means if they believe, they become brothers in religion.
rows.anchor: يعني فإن آمنوا فإخوانكم في الدين

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: The Qummi commentary says to recite and explain the message to the seeker, then leave him alone until he returns to his safe place.
rows.anchor: إقرأ عليه وعرفه ثم لا تتعرض له حتى يرجع إلى مأمنه

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: When asked whether someone could still meet the Prophet after the four months without protection, Ali answered yes and cited the instruction to grant asylum to any polytheist who seeks it.
rows.anchor: يا ابن أبي طالب فمن أراد منا أن يلقى رسول الله في بعض الأمر من بعد انقضاء الأربعة فليس له عهد قال علي بلى

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa said that the people addressed by the command to fight covenant-breakers had not been fought after the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة رضي الله عنه أنهم ذكروا عنده هذه الآية فقال ما قوتل أهل هذه الآية بعد

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa said that by his time only three people from the group of this verse and four hypocrites remained; he identified a few persistent wrongdoers, including one elderly man who could not feel cold water.
rows.anchor: قال كنا عند حذيفة رضي الله عنه فقال ما بقي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: At the Battle of the Camel, Ali asked Basra’s people whether he had ruled unjustly, distributed unfairly, or favored himself and his family; after they denied it, he said the revolt left only disbelief or the sword and applied this verse to them.
rows.anchor: إنهم لأصحاب هذه الآية وما قوتلوا مذ نزلت

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
rows.claim: When Talha and al-Zubayr rebelled, Ali said they had willingly pledged allegiance then broke it without any new offense, and he recited the verse commanding battle against covenant-breaking leaders.
rows.anchor: بايعاني طائعين غير مكرهين ثم نكثا بيعتي من غير حدث احدثته ثم تلا هذه الآية
